$comment: The sweep: flatten everything the hand-written manifest does not cover.
The official ArtAssetID dictionary dates from 2007 and lists ~180 assets.
A real modern skin replaces ~2600. Covering only the documented ones
repaints about 5% of the interface, which reads as 'nothing changed'.
So: skin/dictionary.txt holds the full ID list, and these ordered rules
assign each one a flat colour. First match wins. Anything matching an
Every sweep asset is a SOLID FILL with no border and no 9-slice detail.
That is deliberate: a solid colour looks identical whether the client
stretches, tiles or crops it, so we do not need to know the dimension the
game expects. Assets where a border or a corner actually matters live in
assets.json with their documented size and always take precedence.
Because the fills are solid, all IDs sharing a role point at ONE file.
